Bug 2032569 - Stop browser_history_multiselect.js from racing background history refreshes, r=jsudiaman.

A history refresh rebuilds the sidebar's cards, so the `sidebar-tab-list`
elements and their rows are replaced. The test captured the lists once in
add_setup, then waited for mutations on elements that could by then be detached,
so the waits never resolved and the task timed out. While the cards were being
rebuilt there was no list at that index at all, which is the
`firstList is undefined` failure seen in test-verify. It also counted rows the
previous task had left `selected`, because `resetSelection` clears the tracked
selection but only requests the re-render that drops the attribute.

- Look the lists up right before using them, and wait for a rebuilt list to
  render its rows.
- Wait for the selection to be cleared in the DOM after resetting it, and for
  the focused row through the list rather than for an event on a captured row.
- Wait for the tabs opened by test_open_all_in_tabs to load and flush the
  pending Places writes, so the visits they record are settled there. Every
  waitForNewTab listener resolves on the first TabOpen, so poll for the tabs
  instead of registering one listener per tab.
- Settle the rebuild that removing a page triggers, and assert the selection
  test_open_all_in_tabs_warn depends on, so a missing warning dialog fails on
  that assertion instead of timing out.
- Run the tasks that mutate history after the ones that need a stable row set,
  so their churn cannot land in an unrelated task.

Differential Revision: https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D321494
